what: Decode of twitter.cbor (402814 bytes) into test_binding (values in a std::variant), MiB/s. Arm old: main 131934e+ba2effa, which reads tags 28 and 29 always. Arm off: decode with a template parameter sharedrefs that is off by default, so the code for tags 28 and 29 is not compiled. Arm on: the same header with sharedrefs::on.
why: The owner asked what a default of off would gain for decode.
how: Google Benchmark, one binary per arm, each built twice (a, b). 3 rounds alternating, --benchmark_min_time=0.1s --benchmark_repetitions=3 --benchmark_enable_random_interleaving=true. One warm buffer.
finding: No difference is visible. old 241/237, off 235/211, on 233/240. The two builds of off differ by 10 percent, so the noise of this decode is larger than any effect of the switch.
